title: Stuffed Corn Griddle Cakes with Melted Cheese and Cabbage Relish
summary: These corn masa cakes are stuffed with a gooey melted cheese centre, griddled until spotted golden-brown, and served with a quick tangy cabbage relish and a simple tomato salsa. A classic made easy to shape and cook at home.
equipment: baking tray lined with baking paper
large heavy frying pan or griddle, preferably cast iron

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
boiling water, plus extra warm water as needed
neutral oil, plus extra for the pan
queso fresco or feta, crumbled (check the rennet)
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the curtido
steps.text: Toss the cabbage, carrot, onion, oregano, vinegar, water and the 1/4 teaspoon salt together in a bowl, pressing down firmly to bruise the cabbage. Leave for at least 30 minutes, tossing it now and then, so the salt and vinegar draw out moisture and the cabbage softens and turns pleasantly tangy. The longer it sits, the more mellow and crunchy-tender it becomes, so make this first.

steps.title: Simmer the tomato salsa
steps.text: Blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic and jalapeño until smooth. Warm the oil in a small saucepan over medium heat, add the purée carefully as it will spit, then stir in the 1/4 teaspoon salt and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until it has thickened slightly. This short simmer cooks out the raw tomato edge and lets the flavours settle into a rounder, fuller sauce.

steps.title: Mix and rest the dough
steps.text: Stir the masa harina and 1/4 teaspoon salt together in a bowl, then add the boiling water and 1 teaspoon oil and mix with a spatula into a soft dough. Cover and leave to rest for 20 minutes, which lets the corn flour fully hydrate so the dough becomes easier to shape. Knead briefly for 15-20 seconds, then flatten a small piece to check it: if the edges crack more than a few millimetres, work in warm water a teaspoon at a time until the dough feels soft and slightly tacky, like play dough. Divide into 8 balls of about 85g each and keep them covered under a damp tea towel so they don't dry out and crack.

steps.title: Prepare the cheese filling
steps.text: Mix the mozzarella and queso fresco together in a bowl, then squeeze the mixture into 8 firm balls of about 35g each. Pressing the cheese firmly together now means it holds its shape as a compact filling rather than spilling out of the dough later.

steps.title: Fill and shape the pupusas
steps.text: With damp hands, press a deep dent into a dough ball with your thumb and work it into a small bowl shape with walls about 6mm thick. Drop in one portion of cheese, pull the edges of the dough up and over it and pinch firmly to seal, then roll the parcel gently back into a ball. Pat it between your palms into a disc about 10cm wide and 1.5cm thick, smoothing over any cracks with a wet finger so the cheese can't leak out as it melts. Set it on the lined tray under the damp towel and repeat with the remaining dough and filling.

steps.title: Griddle until golden
steps.text: Heat the heavy frying pan over medium heat and wipe it with a little oil. Cook the pupusas in batches, without crowding the pan, for about 4 minutes per side, until they're browned in patches, crisp at the edges and the cheese inside has fully melted. Drain briefly on kitchen paper, then serve hot with the curtido and tomato salsa alongside, since pupusas lose their crisp edge quickly once they cool.

tips: Check the dough with the crack test before shaping - if the edges split when you flatten a small piece, it's too dry and will tear around the filling, so knead in more warm water a little at a time.
Don't overfill the dough balls; a 35g ball of cheese to an 85g ball of dough leaves enough dough to seal properly without the filling bursting through as it melts.
Keep the heat at medium rather than high - a pan that's too hot browns the outside before the cheese inside has had time to melt through.
Let the curtido sit for the full 30 minutes, or longer if you have time; it needs that time for the vinegar to soften the cabbage properly.
Keep shaped pupusas under a damp towel while you work through the batch, as exposed dough dries out and cracks before it reaches the pan.
storage: Refrigerate cooked pupusas within 1 hour and use within 3 days; reheat in a dry pan over medium-low heat until piping hot (74°C) all the way through. The curtido keeps in the fridge for up to 1 week in a covered container. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
